intro: The real Claude Code desk (Opus 5.5, all eleven agents, the scripts and the order-guard hook) ran headless on real daily prices from 2017. Replay connectors served data only up to each session's date. The harness gave the money rules ($10,000 budget, $2,000 kept aside, $2,500 max per stock) and said yes to each order card. A paper broker filled orders on the real prices that followed.

sessions.prompt:
install skill

My money rules: budget $10,000, keep $2,000 aside as cash, max $2,500 in any one stock. Use the desk defaults for everything else. The Alpaca connector is the paper account (ALPACA_PAPER_TRADE=true).

sessions.result:
**No trade today.** None of the three stocks that passed the screen cleared every gate, so there's no confirmation card and nothing was ordered. The paper account is untouched at $10,000 cash. For this desk, "no trade" counts as a valid outcome.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Setup | Skill installed and your rules saved: $10k budget, $2k kept as cash, $2.5k max per stock, desk defaults otherwise. Alpaca is confirmed as a paper account. |
| Market | **risk_on** (4 of 4 points): the benchmark closed at a 52-week high and VIX is 10.57. QQQ isn't in either connector, so this read comes from SPY and VIX only. |
| Screen | 3 of 14 stocks passed: **BA, V, CSCO**. The others mostly had low trading volume or RSI above 70. |
| **BA** | The plan bought only if BA broke above its 52-week high, so it never got an order. Its **backtest failed**: over 147 trades the rule lost 0.05 R per trade after costs, profit factor 0.94. |
| **V** | **No setup active at Friday's close.** Friday it hit a new high and then reversed lower. The only plan reaching 2:1 was the same breakout rule, which lost money on recent data in a quick test. |
| **CSCO** | **No setup, and the reward is too small:** heavy selling has stopped it at 34.47-34.53 five times, only about 0.4 ATR above the close. Volume patterns also suggest earnings around 05-17/18, which would fall inside the holding period. |

A few things limit how much these results tell you:
- **No news feed:** the replay has none, so news risk is unknown, not clear.
- **Earnings dates are guesses:** they come from volume patterns, not a confirmed calendar.
- **Short price history:** the BA backtest covers 3.9 years, short of the desk's 5-year standard.

I didn't loosen any filters or retune settings to get a pass.

**What could change by next week**
- **CSCO:** a daily close above 34.53 on at least average volume, after the earnings date that the volume pattern suggests.
- **V:** a breakout above 92.98, followed by a pullback where that old high holds as support.
- **AAPL, FB, GOOG:** all are in strong trends but were too stretched (RSI above 70) to pass the screen. A pullback would put them back in range.

I haven't set any price alerts, since there's no plan to watch. I can set them for these levels if you want.

Everything is saved under `trader-workspace/`, in the `screens/`, `plans/`, `backtests/`, `news/` and `regime/` folders. This is decision support on paper, not financial advice.

Three of the 14 names pass the desk's standard filters as of the 2017-05-05 close: BA, V and CSCO. I left the filters unchanged. All three are trend-continuation setups sitting just under their 52-week highs, so the setup is real but crowded right under resistance.

## Survivors (ranked)

| # | Symbol | Score | Setup | Close | RSI14 | ATR% | Rel vol | 3m % | From 52w high |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BA | 60.9 | trend_continuation | 185.01 | 63.3 | 1.15 | 0.96 | +13.9 | -0.38% |
| 2 | V | 50.4 | trend_continuation | 92.09 | 64.5 | 1.03 | 1.06 | +7.0 | -0.96% |
| 3 | CSCO | 42.9 | trend_continuation | 34.39 | 69.4 | 1.05 | 0.93 | +9.8 | -0.41% |

- **BA:** strongest trend in the list. The 50-day average is 179.61 and the 200-day is 154.07, and the 50-day has risen 1.4% over 10 sessions. It closed up 0.93 ATR, at its high for the day. The 52-week high of 185.71 (set 2017-03-02) is only 0.33 ATR above the close, so it is still testing that level, not through it.
- **V:** clean uptrend, and the only survivor with relative volume above 1.0 (1.06). It is weaker than its score suggests. It made a new 52-week high intraday (92.98), then reversed to close at 92.09, down 0.53 ATR on the day, so that high is fresh resistance 0.9 ATR overhead.
- **CSCO:** weakest of the three. RSI is 69.4, just under the 70 cap, so it is stretched. It also has the flattest 50-day average (+0.55% over 10 sessions) and relative volume of 0.93. The 52-week high of 34.53 (2017-03-02) is 0.4 ATR above the close.

- **RSI above 70:** GOOG (84.5, very extended), AAPL (72.1), FB (70.1, just over). All three have strong trends and would be candidates for a pullback entry.
- **RSI above 70 and low relative volume:** HD (RSI 71.5, rel vol 0.64), MSFT (RSI 72.1, rel vol 0.79).
- **Relative volume below 0.8 only:** AMZN (0.79, a near miss), UNH (0.67), CAT (0.70). Their trends are otherwise intact.

- **50-day average not above the 200-day, and low relative volume:** INTC (35.94 vs 35.95, essentially flat, 3-month return +0.8%).

The most common failure is low relative volume (8 names), followed by RSI above 70 (6 names). That reads as a quiet, extended tape, not a weak one. I would not suggest loosening the filters. If anything, AAPL, FB and GOOG are worth watching for a pullback back inside the RSI band.

The plan is a buy-stop-limit order that only fills if BA trades through its 52-week high of 185.71.

| | Price |
|---|---|
| Entry trigger (buy-stop) | 185.85 |
| Entry limit (most we pay) | 186.38 (+0.25 ATR) |
| Stop | 181.70 (just under the 5/1 swing low of 181.80) |

From March to April the stock moved sideways below 185.71. It has risen from the 175.56 low on 4/13 and on Friday reached 185.07, 0.64 below that high. 185.71 is the highest price in the 400 bars on file, so above it there is no known resistance, and the target is simply the 2R level. - A gap open above 187.97 (trigger + 1 ATR) means don't chase; the 186.38 limit won't fill anyway.

agents.report:
**Verdict: FAIL.** The breakout rule behind the BA plan lost money after costs. Over 147 trades it averaged −0.05 R per trade, with a profit factor of 0.94. It should not go to the risk manager.

**Rule tested:** buy on a 20-bar breakout with relative volume of at least 1.0, entering at the next open. Stop at 1.96 × ATR14, target at 2.0 R, and a 20-bar time stop. Costs were the desk defaults: 5 bps slippage and 0.5 bps fees per side, no commission. I ran it once with the analyst's settings. I did not run a variant, because the plan has no obvious error to correct (a stop of about 1.96 ATR is reasonable).

| | All | In-sample | Out-of-sample (from 2016-03-09) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trades | 147 | 91 | 56 |
| Win rate | 40.1% | 35.2% | 48.2% |
| Avg win / avg loss (R) | +1.30 / −0.96 | +1.22 / −1.02 | +1.39 / −0.84 |
| Payoff | 1.35 | 1.19 | 1.66 |
| Expectancy (R/trade) | −0.05 | −0.23 | +0.24 |
| Profit factor | 0.94 | 0.75 | 1.40 |

- **Out-of-sample:** the last 30% of the history was positive, but the rule lost clearly in-sample. A positive result over 56 trades in a strong market (2016-17) is not enough to make up for a losing full sample.
- **Sensitivity:** 4 of 9 nearby settings were profitable, all by tiny amounts (best +0.03 R at stop 2.45 ATR / 2.0 R). No setting nearby reaches the 0.1 R bar, so there is no robust edge at any of them.
- **By symbol:** BA alone made +0.31 R over 20 trades, and MMM made +0.33 R over 19. LMT, HON, UTX, CAT and GE lost, and GD roughly broke even. BA's 20 trades are too few to count, and picking BA because its own chart fit is exactly the curve-fit that pooling the peers is meant to catch.
- **Drawdown and buy-and-hold for BA:** trading BA with this rule returned +5.2% total (1.3% a year), with a maximum drawdown of 3.1% and money in the market 18% of the time. Simply holding BA over the same period returned +84.9%. The rule did not earn its risk compared with holding the stock.
- **Max consecutive losses:** 9.

**Kelly inputs for the position sizer:** win rate 0.401, payoff 1.35, n = 147. These give a negative Kelly fraction, so there should be no position.

**Data source and a shortfall to note:**
- I used TradingView's full chart export, split-adjusted, for BA and seven peers (LMT, GD, HON, UTX, MMM, CAT, GE).
- NOC was not available in TradingView.
- The full histories only go back to 2012-09-04, and an Alpaca check for BA also starts there. That gives 4.7 years of bars, and after warm-up the test covers 3.9 years (2013-06-21 to 2017-05-05). This is short of the 5-year requirement, but it does include the 2015-16 industrials drawdown.
- No one-day move was larger than 15% in any series, so there are no split artifacts.
- The saved bars were merged into `data/BA.csv` and `data/CAT.csv`, replacing their 400-bar versions.
